checks.name: every registered SEQRA-07 source builds a receipt from its committed fixture
re-running a named vintage produces an identical content hash for every source
a missing required SODA field fails the adapter visibly instead of silently parsing
every discovery-probe source records not_a_stable_api and never asserts a row count
actor resolution attributes every demo position to a resolved organization with a source record (A1)
the same raw actor name resolves to the same organization_key across repeated resolution (A1)
resolving an actor with no usable identity throws rather than minting an unstable key
before a second organization's position is public, the issue is named but not yet a coalition or preserved (A2 baseline)
named-issue evidence becomes a measurable coalition once a second organization's position is public (A2)
a later cutoff never surfaces a reaffirmation before it was itself public (A4: no position enters a cutoff before it was public)
a position missing available_to_public_at is refused at construction, never accepted as cutoff-valid (A4 / negative rule)
a position cannot be public before it was observed (A4)
every position from a suppression-required organization type carries a non-empty suppression rule (A3)
no built receipt, position, or derived signal asserts misconduct/motive (A3 / negative rule)
every derived issue-preservation and coalition-continuity signal retains a rival explanation (A5)
resident ingestion remains disabled and every source receipt records it as not committed
the existing SEQRA ontology unit tests for organization/public_position stay green

coalitions.named_issue: shadow impacts on the p s 123 schoolyard
coalitions.rival_explanation: Multiple organizations naming the same issue may share a common information source (a shared advocacy toolkit, a widely circulated notice, or overlapping membership) rather than reflecting independent, uncoordinated agreement; apparent coalition size is not evidence of the issue's technical merit, and it is not a judgment about why any participating organization joined.
coalitions.suppression_rule: This is a process signal about what was formally raised, when, and by how many distinct organizations. It must never be read, displayed, or modeled as a misconduct or motive label for any participating organization, including labor, developer, or community participants.

issues.named_issue: shadow impacts on the p s 123 schoolyard
issues.rival_explanation: The same normalized issue text recurring across positions may reflect independent commenters submitting similar boilerplate language rather than a coordinated or persistent campaign around one preserved concern; this signal does not distinguish the two.
issues.suppression_rule: This is a process signal about what was formally raised, when, and by how many distinct organizations. It must never be read, displayed, or modeled as a misconduct or motive label for any participating organization, including labor, developer, or community participants.
